why_now: What changed in the last 6-12 months (evidence, not narrative): (1) revenue went from Rs 1,019 crore (Q1 FY26) to Rs 1,910 crore (Q1 FY27) and EBITDA from Rs 140 crore to Rs 397 crore, margin 13.7% to 20.8% (e3); (2) data centre mix rose from 1% of FY26 revenue to 21% of Q1 and management expects data centre plus enterprise at about 50% in FY27 (e6); (3) order intake of Rs 13,100 crore in Q1 vs Rs 7,687 crore for all of FY26, including a US$1.11 billion hyperscaler award letter (e5); (4) a Rs 1,500 crore QIP cleared net debt (e8) and CRISIL/ICRA outlooks improved; (5) on 3 Sep 2026 management set a FY29 target of Rs 20,000 crore revenue at 27%+ EBITDA margin (e7). The stock rose about 9x in 12 months (e15), from Rs 104.6 to Rs 969.9, so the evidence suggests most of the visible improvement and a large part of the FY29 plan are already in the price: at about 14x target-year PAT the market is capitalising delivery (i1).
thesis: Evidence suggests STL has moved from a loss-making, tariff-hit fibre maker (FY26 PAT Rs 56 crore, ROCE 9.4%) to a capacity-constrained supplier of high-density cable and connectivity to hyperscalers, with a genuine earnings inflection visible in audited-review numbers and a record order book. This is a real fundamental change, not only a narrative. The open questions are durability and price: the margin gain rests on mix, tariff relief and tight fibre/preform supply that industry capacity additions (Corning, Prysmian, Chinese makers) may erode; one customer now dominates the order book; free cash flow is still small after capex; and the equity trades at 31x Q1 annualised EBITDA. As a 12-24 month multibagger candidate it looks stretched: the plausible upside to the company's own FY29 plan is already largely discounted, while a slowdown in AI spend or an input-cost or tariff shock would hit earnings and the multiple together. Good business momentum, weak asymmetry at this price.
multibagger_mechanism: A plausible path to a 3x+ price would need all of: revenue annualising above Rs 12,000-14,000 crore by FY28 with 25%+ margin (about Rs 3,000-3,500 crore EBITDA, 2x+ Q1 annualised), the market holding a 25-30x earnings multiple on FY29 numbers that exceed management's Lakshya plan, and no supply-driven price normalisation (i4, i1). Math check: a 3x price implies about 43x Lakshya target-year PAT or about 28x target-year EBITDA, so the chain requires both an upgrade of the plan and multiple expansion. The evidence suggests this is a tail outcome (model estimate roughly 3-5% in 24 months), not the base case. A 1.5-2.5x outcome via on-plan execution and a steady multiple is more consistent with the evidence.
expectations_gap: The price (about Rs 50,100 crore market cap) already assumes: Q1 FY27 margin and revenue sustained or exceeded (31x Q1 annualised EBITDA), plus most of the FY29 Lakshya plan (about 14x target-year PAT if met exactly; i1). Management's own risk slide lists AI capex continuity, supply chain, pricing and tariffs as assumptions. The gap that could still favour the stock: if the FY27 EBITDA margin lands near the 23% guidance and revenue run-rate exceeds Rs 8,000 crore, trailing multiples compress quickly through earnings growth even at a flat price; if only the base case happens, the stock has to grow into the multiple and offers limited upside. Reverse arithmetic: to bring EV/EBITDA to 15x at today's EV needs EBITDA of about Rs 3,300 crore, roughly 2.1x the Q1 annualised level.

Price 1.5-3.0x; the 3x end is the tail (about 3-5% model estimate) and needs plan upgrades.

risks: Valuation: about 31x Q1 FY27 annualised EBITDA (32x excluding other income), about 64x annualised PAT and about 56x trailing EBITDA after a roughly 8x rise in 12 months (corrected from 9x, see e15); today's market cap already equals about 14x PAT if the FY29 Lakshya target is delivered (i1) and about 8-9% more on a diluted view (i8). Delivery is likely required just to hold the price.

Customer concentration and contract quality: the US$1.11 billion PAL is about 54% of the Rs 18,618 crore order book (e5) and is an allocation framework with purchase orders released periodically and mutual capped shortfall liabilities of undisclosed size, not a take-or-pay commitment (e16); the Aug and Oct 2026 hyperscaler agreements (US$288 million, ~US$1.2 billion) use the same wording (e17, e18). Whether the 1 Oct LTSA overlaps the PAL is unknown (s2). 'Total potential value' is stated at prevailing selling prices.

Margin quality: the Q1 gain came from operating leverage (gross margin flat at 49.6%, i6) at about 70% utilisation (e21), so it is reversible if volumes or fixed-cost absorption weaken; input costs (germanium, helium, polymers) are already pressuring gross margin.

Plan credibility: Lakshya revenue of Rs 20,000 crore in FY29 is about 22% above what +50% capacity would yield at full utilisation of today's revenue per unit (i7); capex intent moved from Rs 500 crore a year (24 Jul) to Rs 1,000 crore a year, about Rs 3,000 crore in total (e21), funded by 'internal accruals and/or debt'.

AI and hyperscaler capex cyclicality: data-centre mix went from 1% to 21% of revenue in a year; a capex pause or architecture shift (copper/optical mix, hollow-core or co-packaged optics) would hit the highest-margin revenue first (i5). The sector's global leader fell 51% in July 2026 after guiding slightly below expectations (i9, secondary).

Capacity and supply: management admits it must pick orders by capacity (e6); germanium, helium and polymer shortages are not quantified; competitors (Corning US fibre +50%, Prysmian) are adding capacity (e12, e13).

Trade policy: 54% of Q1 revenue is North America; tariffs on Indian-origin goods moved from about 50% to a temporary 10-15% regime and the Lakshya risk slide names tariff continuity as an assumption (e6, e7, e11).

Legal and cash: US$101.25 million Prysmian award under appeal; only the US$41.53 million bond and about Rs 391 crore of restricted cash are set aside, leaving about US$60 million of the award uncovered before interest; two further appeal stages exist; the auditors drew attention to the matter (e9, e24).

Earnings quality and cash: 'net debt-free' status is driven by the Rs 1,500 crore QIP; excluding restricted cash the reported net cash falls from Rs 483 crore to about Rs 92 crore (still including the QIP), and without the QIP the group would be in net debt of about Rs 1,400 crore; FY26 free cash flow after interest was small; Q1 FY27 cash flow is unknown (e8, i3, e10).

Dilution and governance: the QIP (about 5% of shares at Rs 583.01) plus 45.3 million promoter warrants at Rs 110 (about 8.8% of shares; intrinsic value about Rs 3,950 crore at today's price, i8); about Rs 11 crore of FY26 managerial remuneration paid or provided without Schedule V approvals, to go to the AGM (Q1 results note 8). No promoter pledge at 30 Jun 2026 (e22).

Crowding and sentiment: price up 74% since the Q1 print and 8x in 12 months, three upper circuits in September, institutional holding above 33%, retail 15.5% (e22, i11); Indian telecom/network small caps with similar runs have had median 12-month forward ratio of 1.4x and frequent 45-75% drawdowns (i9).

Disclosure hygiene: the 29 Aug LTSA was first attributed to STL and corrected on 31 Aug to a wholly owned subsidiary (e17); the Q1 deck reused FY26 order intake (Rs 7,687 crore) as the FY26-end order book (actual Rs 7,309 crore, e5); v002's price series was misdated by one month (e15). Each is small; together they argue for primary-document checking of every headline number.

Source gaps (not verified): Q1 FY27 and H1 cash flow and working capital; the size of the capped shortfall liabilities and the firm volume in any hyperscaler agreement; hyperscaler identities and PAL/LTSA overlap; total installed capacity; CRISIL/ICRA rating rationales; Q2 FY27 results date; sell-side consensus (only press-reported targets seen).

exit_rules.condition: Consolidated EBITDA margin below 18% in any quarter of FY27 or Q1 FY28 (Q1 FY27 was 20.8%; FY27 guidance 23%; FY26 13.2%).

Quarterly consolidated revenue below Rs 1,500 crore (about 20% under Q1 FY27's Rs 1,910 crore) for two consecutive quarters, or open order book below Rs 15,000 crore without a new award of at least US$300 million.
Optical connectivity attach rate below 20% in the Q2 FY27 presentation, or below 25% / data centre plus enterprise mix below 40% at Q4 FY27 results.
Cancellation, deferral or disclosed volume cut of the US$1.11 billion hyperscaler award letter, or two or more of the four largest US hyperscalers cutting annual capex guidance by 15% or more.

Price above about Rs 1,700 (market cap about Rs 88,000 crore, roughly 25x the Rs 3,500 crore FY29 target-year PAT) without a Lakshya target upgrade or trailing-four-quarter EBITDA above Rs 2,500 crore.
Weekly close below Rs 700 (about 28% under the 2026-10-05 price) triggers an emergency thesis review, not an automatic exit.
Adverse final ruling or settlement above the Rs 391 crore of restricted cash in the Prysmian matter, or an additional equity raise before Q4 FY27 results.

adversarial.strongest_bear_case: The market is paying about Rs 50,500 crore (about 64x annualised earnings, about Rs 55,000 crore counting 45 million promoter warrants issued at Rs 110) for one record quarter whose margin gain came from fixed-cost absorption at about 70% utilisation, not from price. The 'order book' that justifies the multiple is dominated by allocation frameworks with unnamed hyperscalers (US$1.11 billion in May, US$288 million in August, about US$1.2 billion on 1 October) in which purchase orders are released periodically and both sides' shortfall liabilities are capped at undisclosed amounts; none is a take-or-pay commitment, and the October award may simply restate the May one. The FY29 plan (Rs 20,000 crore revenue) exceeds what the stated +50% capacity can produce at today's revenue per unit, the capex doubled in six weeks, and the global leader Corning has already fallen by half from its June peak even on strong results. The stock is up about 8x in 12 months with upper circuits and heavy retail and institutional ownership; STL itself fell 75% after its 2018 peak and 57% after its 2021 peak, and Indian telecom small caps with similar runs had a median 12-month forward ratio of about 1.4x. If call-offs run below allocations, utilisation stays near 70%, input costs persist, or a hyperscaler pauses capex, earnings step back while a 30-60x multiple compresses, which is a 50%+ drawdown path.

questions.what_evidence_would_make_it_wrong: Some has already appeared: the hyperscaler awards are allocation frameworks with capped, undisclosed shortfall liabilities (e16-e18), not firm orders; gross margin was flat so the 20.8% EBITDA margin is operating leverage (i6); and the FY29 revenue target exceeds the stated capacity plan at today's revenue per unit (i7). Still pending: Q2 FY27 EBITDA margin below about 18%, quarterly revenue below Rs 1,500 crore, attach rate below 20%, disclosure of the shortfall caps or hyperscaler call-offs below allocation, a negative H1 operating cash flow, or a hyperscaler capex cut (see the armed exit rules).
questions.what_is_missing: Q1 and H1 cash flow and working capital (the first cash-flow statement is due with the Q2 results); the firm volume and cap size in each hyperscaler agreement; hyperscaler identities and whether the 1 Oct LTSA is the definitive form of the 22 May PAL (s2); absolute installed capacity; gross margin by segment (data centre vs telecom); sell-side consensus numbers; the Q2 results date. Not verified: the CRISIL/ICRA rating rationales and the content of the 28 Sep 2026 analyst meet (no transcript seen).
questions.is_catalyst_priced_in: Largely yes for the known catalysts. The stock rose from Rs 564 on the Q1 print (24 Jul) to Rs 982 (5 Oct), +74%, through the Lakshya event (three-plus upper circuits, Rs 713 on 3 Sep to Rs 897 on 11 Sep) and the 1 Oct award (+5.0% on 2.8x normal volume); press-reported broker targets of Rs 950-1,100 (Jul-Sep) are at or just above the price (i11). What is not priced is the cash conversion and the Q2 margin test, which could cut either way.
questions.does_valuation_fit_growth: Only if the plan is delivered. 64x annualised PAT and 31x EBITDA (8-9% higher on a diluted basis, i8) are about 14x the Lakshya FY29 PAT, but Lakshya needs 4.2x revenue and 27% margin, and revenue 22% above the stated capacity plan at today's revenue per unit (i7). FY26 ROCE was 9.4% and FY26 PAT Rs 56 crore (e4, e10), so the earnings record is one quarter old. The valuation fits the growth only with full delivery and an undiminished multiple, with no margin for error.
questions.great_company_vs_great_stock: The evidence suggests an improving company (integrated glass-to-gigabit, AA rating from Crisil in Sep 2026 (e23), patent dispute with Fujikura closed in its favour on 3 Jul, Q1 PAT Rs 197 crore) and a stretched stock. At this price the question is stock, not company: the author's own scenarios (bull 20%, base 45%, bear 35%) imply an expected 24-month multiple of roughly 1.1x, near or below a cost-of-equity hurdle.
questions.merely_an_ai_narrative: No: the revenue evidence is real (Q1 revenue Rs 1,910 crore, data-centre 21% of revenue, PAT Rs 197 crore on limited-review accounts, e3, e6). But the forward leg is narrative-adjacent: the three hyperscaler agreements total about US$2.6 billion of 'potential value' on allocation terms (e16-e18), and about 79% of Q1 revenue was still not data-centre (telecom, enterprise and rural), with a group EBITDA margin of 13.2% in FY26 before the data-centre mix.
questions.is_it_crowded: Moderately to highly. Institutions above 33% post-QIP, FPIs 18.2%, mutual funds 9.5%, retail up to Rs 2 lakh 15.5% (e22); three consecutive upper circuits in September and an RSI of 74.5 (i11); the lab's own momentum screen ranks it 2 (e2); and the stock is up about 8x in 12 months. The global leader's 51% fall in July (i9, secondary) shows how fast the optical theme can reverse.
questions.strongest_bear_argument: You pay about Rs 50,500 crore for one quarter of operating-leverage margin and an order book made of allocation frameworks with capped, undisclosed shortfall liabilities; the plan exceeds the stated capacity, capex doubled in six weeks, and if hyperscaler call-offs, utilisation or input costs disappoint, earnings fall while a 30-60x multiple de-rates, as it did after STL's 2018 and 2021 peaks (-75%, -57%). See strongest_bear_case.
questions.what_happened_in_similar_setups: Mixed but sobering (i9, own computation on Yahoo prices, biased sample). STL 2017-19: 4.3x then -75%. STL 2020-22: 4.9x then -57%. RailTel and ITI: about 6x then -57% to -59%. Optiemus: 3.7x then -66%, later recovered. Corning 1999-2002: 3.7x then -96%. Continuations also exist (HFCL 2020-21 about 3x more, Tejas and Tanla 2020-21). Across 19 Indian episodes since 2013 the median 12-month forward ratio was 1.4x with 8 of 19 below 1.0x. I found no good analogue where an unfunded-cash-flow capex doubling followed a multi-fold run without a drawdown.
questions.what_must_happen_for_5x: A 5x is Rs 4,910 a share, about Rs 252,000 crore of market cap (Rs 275,000 crore diluted). That needs PAT of Rs 10,000-11,000 crore at 25x or Rs 6,300-6,900 crore at 40x, versus about Rs 3,500 crore in the Lakshya FY29 plan (i10). Operationally: revenue far above Rs 20,000 crore at 27%+ margin, reached before Oct 2028, with the market still paying 25-40x; or 70x on the plan.
questions.is_5x_plausible_in_1_2_years: No: the model estimate is below 1% within 24 months (and the author's 3x tail of about 3-5% looks generous given i7). A more realistic 24-month range is about 0.35x to 2.0x with the central tendency near 1.0x: on-plan delivery at 20-25x PAT supports roughly 1.4-1.7x (about 2x at 28x), half the plan about 0.7x, an AI-capex pause or de-rating 0.35-0.65x.
questions.probability_market_already_right: Model estimate 50-60% that the price already roughly discounts the realistic outcome distribution (expected 24-month return near or below the cost of equity). Reasons: the inflection is real and verified, but the price already capitalises most of the plan (14x FY29 PAT only if delivered), the plan looks stretched against capacity, order quality is weaker than the headline, and there is a visible 40-50% downside path for a modest miss; the offsetting upside is a second-half margin above 23% and firm call-offs.

Yahoo Finance daily chart API (aggregator, price context only; not independently cross-checked to NSE bhavcopy). Does not change the conclusion that the stock has re-rated several-fold.

evidence.claim: Valuation arithmetic (model): market cap about Rs 50,123 crore (Level-1 snapshot) and EV about Rs 49,600 crore using reported net cash. EV/EBITDA is about 31x on Q1 FY27 annualised EBITDA (397 x 4 = 1,588), about 56x on trailing four quarters (141+129+218+397 = 885) and about 79x on FY26 (628). P/E is about 64x on Q1 annualised PAT (197 x 4 = 788) and about 206x on trailing PAT (4-17+59+197 = 243). If the FY29 Lakshya target is met exactly (revenue 20,000, EBITDA 27% = 5,400) and depreciation is about 650, interest about 100 and tax 25%, PAT is about Rs 3,500 crore, so today's market cap is about 14x that PAT and today's EV about 9x that EBITDA. A 3x price (market cap about Rs 150,000 crore) would be about 43x target-year PAT or about 28x target-year EBITDA.
evidence.note: Derived from e3, e7, e8, e15; depreciation, interest and tax are my assumptions. Trailing figures use FY26 quarterly numbers from the Q4 deck (e4, e11).

evidence.claim: Concentration (model): the US$1.11 billion award is spread over FY27-FY29 (about Rs 3,300 crore a year on a Rs 10,000+ crore value), which is roughly 40-45% of the Q1 FY27 annualised revenue of about Rs 7,640 crore and more than half of the Rs 18,618 crore order book. FY26 had no customer above 10% of revenue (e10). The evidence suggests customer concentration is rising from low to high within a year, and the award letter's volume commitments are not disclosed.
evidence.note: Derived from e5, e10, e3.

evidence.claim: Earnings quality (model): FY26 operating cash flow of about Rs 520 crore less capex of Rs 193 crore less finance costs of Rs 224 crore leaves little free cash; the reported 'net debt-free' status at Q1 FY27 is mostly the Rs 1,500 crore QIP. Excluding the QIP money and the Rs 391 crore restricted cash, net cash of Rs 483 crore implies net debt of roughly Rs 1,400 crore before the raise, so the balance sheet repair is equity-funded, not yet cash-flow-funded. Q1 FY27 cash flow is not disclosed in the sources read.
evidence.note: Derived from e8, e10, and the Q1 FY27 results (e3).

evidence.claim: Mechanism chain (model): (a) hyperscaler/data-centre mix rising from 1% to 21% of revenue lifts EBITDA margin from 13.2% (FY26) to 20.8% (Q1 FY27); (b) the order book (e5) and attach-rate and capacity plans (e6, e7) support revenue of Rs 7,600 crore+ annualised; (c) management targets Rs 20,000 crore and 27% margin by FY29 (e7). Each link is stated by management, none is independently verified, and the market cap already capitalises most of (c) at about 14x target-year PAT (i1). A several-fold outcome would need targets above management's own plan, a higher multiple, or both.
evidence.note: Derived from e3, e5, e6, e7, i1.

evidence.claim: If AI or data-centre capex slows (model scenario): a reversal of most of the margin gain would take EBITDA margin toward the FY26 level of about 13-14%; on Q1 annualised revenue of about Rs 7,600 crore that is about Rs 1,000-1,100 crore of EBITDA vs Rs 1,588 crore annualised, a drop of about a third, while about Rs 1,000 crore a year of planned capex and a customer base concentrating into a few hyperscalers raise fixed-cost and renewal risk. Industry capacity is also rising (Corning US fibre +50%, Prysmian capacity increase). With a 30-50x trailing multiple, a de-rating plus lower earnings is consistent with a drawdown well above 50%. Telecom and BharatNet/BEAD demand (about 80% of FY26 revenue) is the cushion, but it carried a 13% margin.
evidence.note: Derived from e4, e6, e7, e12, e13. Percentages are model estimates, not forecasts.

evidence.claim: SPECULATION: spot-linked fibre prices (CRU, e14) and management commentary that spot is 15-20% above long contracts could normalise if Chinese and Western capacity additions arrive in 2027-2028, compressing the pricing that supports today's margins. Timing is unknown.
evidence.note: No source supports a date; carries no weight in the thesis.

evidence.claim: Exchange filing 22 May 2026: a subsidiary of STL received a Product Award Letter (PAL) from 'a hyperscale partner' for multi-year supply of optical connectivity products, 'total potential value ... estimated at ~USD 1.11 billion ... based on prevailing selling prices'. Terms: allocation of products in each financial year FY27 to FY29; purchase orders 'will be released periodically'; 'reciprocal risk-sharing framework by defining mutual, capped financial liabilities for both parties in the event of demand shortfalls or supply capacity shortages'; executable up to March 2029.
evidence.note: This is the only primary disclosure of the PAL's terms. It is an allocation framework with capped (amount undisclosed) liabilities on both sides; firm volume is not stated.

evidence.claim: Exchange filing 29 Aug 2026: long-term supply agreement with 'a leading hyperscaler' for high-density optical fibre cable, approximately US$288 million, allocation in each calendar year 2027 to 2029, purchase orders released periodically, same 'mutual, capped financial liabilities' language for demand shortfalls or supply capacity shortages. A 31 Aug 2026 clarification states the agreement was executed by a wholly owned subsidiary, not by STL as first stated.
evidence.note: Clarification: https://nsearchives.nseindia.com/corporate/STLTECH_31082026181519_Clarification_LTA_280826_signed.pdf (a disclosure-quality blemish, not a financial item). Not in the v002 thesis.

evidence.note: Disconfirming-the-bear evidence recorded for balance: credit quality is improving.

evidence.claim: FY26 consolidated audited report (annual report): the auditors' report draws attention (Emphasis of Matter) to the Prysmian litigation against the US subsidiary (Note 39(4)); the note states the award of US$101.25 million, the appeal to the Fourth Circuit, a US$41.53 million bond, and that the financial implications 'cannot be ascertained'. No provision for the award is described in the text read.
evidence.note: The PDF is two-column and the auditor's paragraph extracted interleaved; the Emphasis of Matter wording was reconstructed from the extracted text and is flagged as such. Uncovered exposure = US$101.25 million award less the US$41.53 million bond, before post-judgment interest.

evidence.claim: Source of the Q1 margin (model): gross margin (revenue less materials consumed and change in inventories) was 49.6% in Q1 FY27 vs 49.7% in Q1 FY26 and 50.1% in Q4 FY26, i.e. flat. EBITDA margin rose from 13.7% to 20.8% because employee cost fell from 15.3% to 10.2% of revenue and other expenses from 21.4% to 19.2%. The evidence suggests the gain is operating leverage on a largely fixed cost base (consistent with utilisation of about 70%, e21), not a price or mix uplift; the CFO said gross margin was under input-cost pressure. STL also says it does not sell in the spot market (Q4 FY26 call), so it has less direct exposure to the spot fibre-price spike than HFCL.
evidence.note: Derived from e3 (expense lines in the NSE results PDF: materials 805, inventory change +158, employee 195, other 367) and the Q1 call. This challenges the v002 mechanism step (a) in i4 that mix lifted the margin.

evidence.claim: Plan vs capacity (model): Q1 FY27 annualised revenue is about Rs 7,640 crore at 'about 70%' utilisation (e21), implying about Rs 10,900 crore at full utilisation of today's capacity at today's prices and mix; +50% capacity by end FY29 implies about Rs 16,400 crore at full utilisation. The Lakshya FY29 revenue target of Rs 20,000 crore (e7) is about 22% above that, so it needs higher realisations, a much richer connectivity mix (value added without fibre capacity), or capacity beyond what is stated. Not reconcilable from the documents.
evidence.note: Derived from e3, e7, e21. Caveats: utilisation basis unknown (likely physical); pre-terminated connectivity and DC solutions add revenue per fibre-km; the Rs 3,000 crore plan includes a greenfield connectivity plant. The arithmetic is a plausibility test, not a forecast.

evidence.claim: Dilution not in the headline multiples (model): 45.3 million promoter warrants at Rs 110 equal about 8.8% of the 513.9 million post-QIP shares. The Rs 110 exercise price is close to the 2 Feb 2026 close of Rs 110.3 (consistent with an early-February reference date; the pricing basis is not stated in the documents read), but the stock was Rs 166.9 on the 4 Mar EGM and Rs 176.4 on allotment day (Yahoo daily).

evidence.claim: Analogues (model, from Yahoo daily closes; selection and survivorship bias apply): STL itself rose 4.3x from Jan 2017 to a Jan 2018 peak of Rs 410 then fell 75% to Rs 104 by Aug 2019, and rose 4.9x from Mar 2020 to an Aug 2021 peak of Rs 312 then fell 57% to Rs 133 by Jul 2022. RailTel (6.2x to Jul 2024) fell 59% by Mar 2026; ITI (6.2x to Jan 2025) fell 57% by Apr 2025; Optiemus (3.7x to Sep 2024) fell 66% by Mar 2026 then recovered to about Rs 800. Corning, the global fibre leader, peaked at US$255.7 on 29 Jun 2026 (6.5x from a US$39.1 low on 4 Apr 2025) and fell 51% to US$124.1 by 29 Jul 2026 after reporting strong Q2 results but guiding Q3 slightly below expectations (secondary reports), and had recovered to about US$164 by 2 Oct. Corning rose about 3.7x from mid-1999 to a June 2000 peak and then fell 96% by mid-2002. Base rate across 19 episodes since 2013 in eight Indian telecom/network small caps (STL, HFCL, ITI, RailTel, Optiemus, Vindhya Telelinks, Tanla, Tejas): price 12 months after the first date the 12-month gain reached 3x had a median ratio of 1.40x, 8 of 19 below 1.0x, 4 of 19 at or above 3x, 1 of 19 at or above 5x.
evidence.note: Own computation on Yahoo daily series (STLTECH.NS, HFCL.NS, ITI.NS, RAILTEL.NS, OPTIEMUS.NS, VINDHYATEL.NS, TANLA.NS, TEJASNET.NS, GLW); older prices may be split/demerger-adjusted by the vendor; names were chosen by me so the sample is not random. Corning drop context: Nasdaq/247WallSt-type secondary reports; the cause is not verified in primary sources.

evidence.claim: What a 5x needs (model): Rs 4,910 a share is a market cap of about Rs 252,000 crore (Rs 275,000 crore diluted). At 25x earnings that needs PAT of about Rs 10,100-11,000 crore; at 40x, about Rs 6,300-6,900 crore. v002's own Lakshya FY29 PAT estimate is about Rs 3,500 crore (i1), so a 5x needs 1.8-3.1x the company's target-year profit, or 70x+ on the plan, inside 24 months when FY29 has not yet occurred. On the plan delivered exactly and a 20-25x multiple the value is roughly Rs 70,000-88,000 crore (1.4-1.7x); on half the plan at 20x roughly 0.7x.
evidence.note: Derived from i1, e15, i8. Probability of a 5x in 24 months: model estimate below 1%.
